# Avaz

> Avaz is open-source text-to-speech that runs on the device itself: in the browser or on an ordinary CPU, with no server. We are building it for natural intonation on phones. Today it speaks Azerbaijani and English; Turkish and Russian are next. The text never leaves the device; no sign-up.

- Languages: Azerbaijani is the project's own model, "Inflect-Micro-v2 Azerbaijani", a 9.36M-parameter VITS model (24 kHz, one voice) that started as a fine-tune of owensong/Inflect-Micro-v2 by Owen Song. The current checkpoint, v2.1, continues from the first on audio distilled from a teacher TTS, with a stress frontend on top of eSpeak NG; the browser playground runs v2.1 too. English is that base model, unmodified. Turkish and Russian are planned next, with no dates. Avaz is the project's name; the repository, Space and model ids keep the name Inflect_Micro_v2_Azerbaijan.
- The browser playground needs no install: type text, press Speak, download a WAV. Up to 500 characters at a time; profanity is replaced with a bleep. The first visit downloads about 37 MB; after that it works offline.
- It reads Azerbaijani numbers, dates, percentages and currency the way a person says them aloud ("25%" -> "iyirmi beş faiz", "19,99 AZN" -> "on doqquz manat doxsan doqquz qəpik").
- Speed: on a laptop CPU the Python package runs 2-4x faster than real time. In the browser, WebGPU (Chrome, Edge on a computer) is faster than real time. A phone browser usually runs it on the CPU (WebAssembly, int8 decoder), where a sentence can take up to a minute.
- Status, honestly: not there yet. The model is small and fast, but its intonation is still flat, especially over long sentences (text is cut into chunks of about 15 words for that reason), and phone browsers run it slowly. Yes/no questions end with falling pitch instead of a rise. Some consonants are confused (m->n, b->d, q->k), most often in a sentence's first and last word. Corrected stress is carried by length, not yet by pitch. The fixed 6 kHz ring of the first checkpoint is gone, but harmonic clarity at 2-4 kHz is below the teacher's. One voice, no emotion control, no voice cloning. The Azerbaijani training audio is synthetic, distilled from a teacher TTS, which caps the quality. Text is expected in the Latin alphabet.
- Licence: the code and both checkpoints are Apache-2.0. The phonemiser (eSpeak NG, and phonemizer on the Python side) is GPL-3.0-or-later: running it is unrestricted, but redistributing a combined work brings GPL-3.0 obligations. The model accepts pre-phonemised input (`accepts_prephonemized_input`), which is the way out. The Azerbaijani dataset the model was first trained on (ughurabbasov/azerbaijani-tts-dataset) is used with its author's permission, on condition of attribution. The English voice is synthetic and Apache-2.0, but open-weight, not open-data. Not legal advice.
- Not permitted: impersonating a real person or producing deceptive content.

## Try it

- [Playground on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ilqarrrr/Inflect_Micro_v2_Azerbaijan): the page itself, running in the browser
- [About Avaz, in English](https://ilqarrrr-inflect-micro-v2-azerbaijan.static.hf.space/about-en.html): the goal, languages, weak spots, how it works and a FAQ
- [About Avaz, in Azerbaijani](https://ilqarrrr-inflect-micro-v2-azerbaijan.static.hf.space/about.html): the same page in Azerbaijani

## Use it in code

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/HuseynliIlqar/Inflect_Micro_v2_Azerbaijan): the `aztts` Python library, the `say.py` command line, tests and the training pipeline
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HuseynliIlqar/Inflect_Micro_v2_Azerbaijan/main/README.md): setup, command line, Python API, licence and commercial use
- [Model weights on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/ilqarrrr/Inflect_Micro_v2_Azerbaijan): PyTorch and ONNX
